en: Haha, my real name's fine. Only little boys who can't tell the gas from the brakes get stuck with the Meteor treatment.
Tell me, why did you want to race me?
There's only one reason I ever make a challenge. To see who's fastest.
And, I guess that's you. A guy. Thanks for demolishing my perfect record.
You really hate losing to men, huh?
That's right. I told you the nightlife industry's dominated by men, didn't I? Same with the racing community.
It's always a man behind the wheel. The girl just sits in the passenger's seat like an ornament. That's what everyone thinks.
I, for one, can't stand being put in a box. So I took it upon myself to show up anyone who tries, whether their target is me or anyone else.
Anyway. I've always been into cars. So I came up with this idea for a group where women can thrive, and it turned into the Vixen Zeroes.
I see. And you've kept up the struggle to gain women some recognition ever since?
Uh-huh. I just wish I didn't have to bust my ass so hard only for some taxi-driving <Italic>dude</Italic> to leave me in the dust.
Everyone'll probably go dunking on us all over again... After all, we're just girls.
Look... I know you're disappointed, but that doesn't mean you have to start from square one. You've already built up quite a name for yourselves.
And it certainly doesn't matter what any frustrated male critic says. That only shows their ignorance of what it truly means to be a man.
What matters is you⑬a woman who can drive like the wind. A street racer with integrity. Win or lose, I think you at least deserve credit for that. So give yourself some.
Yeah... I guess there is that. Sometimes I get so caught up with fighting the good fight, I forget how far I've come. Happens when you're a girl with a goal.
...Haha, now I'm glad we met, and got to put our racing to the test. Oh, and this is to make up for that drink. Don't feel bad about taking it.
Congrats, Suzuki-san. That's the first time I ever said that to a man and meant it. So yay for you.

If every guy were as understanding as you, the world would
be much better off. Be nice if they were as handsome, too.
Heh, you don't have to say all that.
...In any case, I gotta get going.
It really was a pleasure to race you. Thanks for accepting the challenge.
So... Do you plan on doing more racing from here on out?
Not sure yet. For some reason, our race helped me get a lot out of my system. I'll probably take a break for a while before I get back to it.
Oh, but if I ever do start yearning for some high-octane action, I can just catch a ride in your taxi, right? Hope you won't mind! Hahaha.
(Rena Nanami, the Spangled Meteor... Now that's a badass lady.)
(Damn... I lost.)
Suzuki-san. I've brought word from the Spangled Meteor.
She doesn't believe you were trying your hardest today. She wants another bout with you, and says next time you'd better give it your all.
If you slack off just because you're racing a girl, you'll only get crushed again. So give her the rematch she deserves.
When you feel like taking on the Spangled Meteor, just come and see me. I'll be waiting, Suzuki-san.
(That's the Spangled Meteor!)
(The only way to actually see one of the Vixen Zeroes is to beat them in a race.)
(I've got to win this time!)
(I guess I'll have to give this a shot!)
Hey, you're going to blow our cover if you get any closer! Put some distance between us, quick!
You're way too close! Ease off some more!
Fall back a little more.
Heheh. She'll never spot me back here.
Hey, we'll lose sight of Ryoko-chan if you don't get closer!
If you fall back any further we'll lose them! Hurry up and close the gap!
All right. Nice work! Now I'll know where Ryoko lives. Hehehe.
Aww, I can't see Ryoko-chan any more.
Come on, you're supposed to be tailing her!
Hehehe. I'll see you soon, sweet little Ryoko-chan!
Please, come quick before he's killed!
Over here! Please, before it's too late!
No more. I'm begging you!
No, you should still have some fight left. You're still breathing, aren't you?
But my arm's broken! You win!
You're not getting out of this that easy.
Hey, lay off him.
You're Raiden, right?
Heh. Well if it isn't Kazuma Kiryu.
He's had enough, Raiden. Or do you plan on killing him?
He's a Victory Road competitor, and it's a no-holds-barred tournament. Anything goes.
So yes, I plan on killing him.
No, don't! Please!
That's enough! You've already won this battle!
No, it's not over yet.
Aaaaaah!!!
That cracking sounded like a spinal injury. He'll be wheelchair-bound for the rest of his life. See? <Italic>Now</Italic> this fight is over.
You monster...
Is life really that precious? Is that what they teach you Japanese people in school?
The truth is, there're places where human life is worth less than garbage⑬including the country where I was born.
It's a place of endless civil war where children are abducted from their villages and forced to join the rebel army.
Their parents are slaughtered, and if the kids don't cooperate, they too are murdered. But a sure death also awaits on the battlefield.
It's kill or be killed on the battlefield, and there's no escape. Try to flee, and you'll just die tired. Being from the wrong tribe is also a death sentence.
But the battlefield is where I was raised. I survived by killing. I lived through hell to get stronger.
Find some other shoulder to cry on. I have no sympathy for someone like you.
Cry? Hell, I'm ready to celebrate. Rich bastards are paying good money to watch me rip out some unlucky asshole's guts. What's not to like?
And here in Japan, even the most worthless of lives fetch a nice bounty. Hehe. I'm laughing all the way to the bank.
Well, Kazuma Kiryu? Care to be my next victim?
I'll take you on, if that's what you mean.
Please wait.
Very impressive, Raiden-san. Your win here has advanced you through the qualifying round.
You've made it to the Victory Road finals.
Raiden was right. It is perfectly acceptable to kill your opponent in this competition.
However, we can't have tournament finalists fighting outside the ring. We have to save that for the paying customers.
Bah, looks like we'll have to settle this in the ring.
Don't you go running away now, Kazuma Kiryu. I've set my sights on you.
Have you heard about Raiden's performance so far?
His qualifying round opponents will never fight again. They'll be lucky if they can even lead a normal life.
Raiden has mastered many martial arts and proven himself in underground fighting scenes around the world. And he's a merciless killer.
We've been holding Victory Road qualifiers across Japan trying to find fighters like him.
And thanks to him, we've been able to weed out the less impressive entrants who could not possibly satisfy our clientele.
I suppose so.
You should call an ambulance for this guy.
Oh, I assure you, it has already been arranged.
Now then, with Raiden's advancement, the Victory Road finals, the first new Coliseum championship tournament, will be held shortly.
We have all the contenders we need now. Sixteen of the best fighters throughout Japan.
The Victory Road tournament has sought out the best of the best. Only the absolute strongest have made it this far.
We request your presence at the Underground Coliseum down in Purgatory. Please do not delay. Our clientele thirsts for blood.
(The Victory Road finals... It's time to stop that maniac Raiden.)
Shoulda known you'd be competing, too.
This is really shaping up to be an epic battle.
Man, how in the world did I get mixed up in this?
Anyone seen Raiden?
Raiden? What's that?
Some foreigner. Word is he beats the shit outta his opponents even when he don't have to. Their fightin' days are over after him.
Kiryu-san, is there any particular reason you ask about him?
Raiden's mine. Don't take this personally, but I'm not going to hold back against anyone, not even you, till I finish him off.
Hehe. You mean you don't want any of your friends getting killed.
Raiden.
Speak of the devil.
The real fun's about to begin, Kazuma Kiryu. But the only one laughing at the end is going to be me.
Now that everyone's here...
Let's see who'll be the last man standing. There's only one way to find out.
It's a little too hot in here.
Yeah, I'll go ahead and do that.
What? Don't you think that's a little harsh?
That'd be good. Thanks.
Fine. Ignore me, then.
People often walk out in front of you on roads like this. It always makes me nervous.
But what if you hit someone!?
Good. That sets my mind at ease.
Mistakes? Does that mean what I think it means?
There are lots of people around here today. Don't you worry you might hit someone?
I'm glad you're confident.
Um... You sure you should be driving?
Yet?
What do you focus on while working?
What!? You're scaring me.
(What's with this email? Some kinda mistake?)
(Guess I'll check it out when I get time.)
(What could this email be about? Was it sent to me by mistake?)
(It does sound interesting, though. Maybe I'll take a look if I find time.)
(Who's this email from? I think they sent it to the wrong guy.)
(Well, I'll look into it when I get a chance.)
(Huh... What's this email about? Did they send it to the wrong person?)
(I guess I'll look into it when I have time.)
First, there's a knack to using the accelerator.
Could be a red light. Careful with the brakes.
You all settled in at work now?
Yes. I've pretty much learned the ropes.
I'm still trying to get the hang of things.
Don't worry, you'll get there.
I have no idea what I'm doing.
Hm. Well, I hope you find your feet soon.
Hey, don't ignore the question!
Watch for the stop sign up ahead.
Looks like we're almost there.
Thank you, Uncle Kaz! The parfait was yummy!
Aw. I wanted to eat that.
Uncle Kaz! Can you get me a <Color:8>Strawberry Parfait<Color:Default>, please?
(Looks like Haruka wants a <Color:8>Strawberry Parfait<Color:Default>.)
Thanks, Uncle Kaz! That hamburger was super delicious!
Aw, but I wanted that.
